svg.desc: Left: contiguous allocation reserves the maximum length for each of three sequences, and most of each reservation is never used. Right: paged attention stores each sequence's KV cache in 16-token blocks scattered across GPU memory, found through a per-sequence block table; free blocks can serve any sequence. The KV cache per token is 2 times layers times KV heads times head dimension times bytes.

svg.text: Paged attention: KV cache in blocks

svg.text: Reserve-the-maximum wastes memory; fixed-size blocks allocated on demand do not.

svg.text: GPT-2 small, fp16: 2 × 12 × 12 × 64 × 2 = 36,864 B ≈ 36 KB per token; a 7B model without GQA: 512 KB.

svg.text: The KV cache, not the weights, limits how many sequences fit; paging lets many more fit and lets sequences share a common prefix.
